LESSON: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.5: Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should words be spelt correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. spell commonly misspelt words correctly
2. use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing
3. write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Spell commonly misspelt words correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to spell commonly misspelt words correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: spell commonly misspelt words correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can spell commonly misspelt words correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing

What this means
In this part you learn to use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: spell commonly misspelt words correctly)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing to a partner. (skill: use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: spell commonly misspelt words correctly.
3. Practise this skill: use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing.
4. Practise this skill: write words with silent vowels (-ie and -ei) correctly.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should words be spelt correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: spell commonly misspelt words correctly.
5. Be able to: use prefixes and suffixes correctly in writing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
